originalAbstract:
Introduction

Metallic orbital foreign bodies may pose a safety risk during magnetic resonance imaging due to potential displacement or heating of ferromagnetic material within the magnetic field, potentially resulting in severe ocular injury. When their presence cannot be reliably excluded based on patient history, imaging is performed as a precautionary screening step prior to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Digital radiography (DR) is commonly used for this purpose due to its low radiation dose but provides limited anatomical and spatial information. Photon-counting CT (PCCT) offers high spatial resolution and improved dose efficiency and may serve as an alternative ultra-low-dose screening technique. This phantom study compared radiation exposure between DR and ultra-low-dose PCCT for orbital imaging.

Methods

Orbital imaging was performed in an Alderson RANDO phantom using DR and PCCT. Absorbed radiation doses to the eye lens and globe were measured using optically stimulated luminescence dosimeters (OSLDs) and effective doses were estimated from standard dose descriptors and compared for both modalities.

Results

Mean absorbed doses of PCCT imaging were 0.092 mGy for the lens and 0.087 mGy for the globe, compared with 6.215 mGy and 4.855 mGy for DR, corresponding to dose reductions of 98.5% and 98.2%. Effective doses were 0.002 mSv for PCCT and 0.023 mSv for DR, corresponding to a 91.3% reduction.

Conclusion

Ultra-low-dose PCCT substantially reduced ocular radiation exposure compared with DR while allowing visualization of the tested metallic foreign body. Further studies are warranted to evaluate its diagnostic performance as a dose-saving alternative for orbital foreign body screening prior to MRI.

Implication for practice

Ultra-low-dose PCCT may represent a dose-saving alternative for orbital foreign body imaging prior to MRI, with the additional benefit of cross-sectional visualization. Further validation of diagnostic performance is required before routine clinical implementation.

title: MRI-guided HDR brachytherapy or integrated VMAT boost for tumour-targeted dose escalation in localised prostate cancer: long-term results of the TARGET study.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate local control of the gross tumour volume in localised prostate cancer following focal dose escalation delivered by integrated boost volumetric modulated arc therapy (IB-VMAT) or high-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy. Materials and methods Patients with localised prostate cancer and an intraprostatic lesion identified on multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) were included in a prospective, non-randomised phase II study. Eighty patients received VMAT to the prostate 76 Gy/38 fractions. Boost strategy involved an IB of 95 Gy/38 fractions (IB-VMAT) or a single fraction of 10 Gy (HDR-VMAT). Three patients received 6 months androgen deprivation therapy. The primary endpoint was 3-year local control (LC) assessed by MRI or MRI-guided biopsy. Secondary outcomes included biochemical failure-free survival (bFFS), toxicity and health-related quality of life (HRQoL), assessed using CTCAE v.4.0, the American Urological Association Symptom Score and EPIC. Results Median follow-up was 4.8 years (IQR, 4.0-8.0). Sixty-six patients underwent a 3-year MRI or MRI-guided biopsy; one patient demonstrated recurrence within the boost volume. Four patients demonstrated intraprostatic failure outside the boost volume and three patients developed regional/distant metastases. Eight patients experienced biochemical failure (4 IB-VMAT; 4 HDR-VMAT). Overall, 5-year bFFS was 86.9% (95% CI, 79.1-95.5). No substantial differences in late toxicities and HRQoL were observed between cohorts. Conclusion Intraprostatic tumour-targeted dose escalation using IB-VMAT or HDR-VMAT provided high rates of LC and bFFS with limited adverse impact in late toxicity and HRQoL. Randomised studies are needed to further define the merits and differences between the two techniques.

title: A prospective randomized evaluation of AI assisted GTV contouring in head-and-neck radiotherapy.
abstract: Background AI-assisted contouring has demonstrated efficiency and consistency benefits for organs-at-risk in radiotherapy. However, its impact on gross tumor volume (GTV) delineation remains unexplored. The aim of this study was to evaluate AI-assisted GTV contouring in head and neck cancer radiotherapy in an exploratory randomized controlled clinical trial. Methods In this prospective, single-centre, randomized controlled evaluation, patients referred for curative-intent radiotherapy of head-neck cancer were randomized to manual contouring (control) or AI-assisted contouring (intervention) of gross tumor volumes using an in-house developed segmentation model. The primary endpoint was the extent of editing during a blinded multidisciplinary target conference, using normalized Added Path Length (APL). Secondary endpoints included conference duration, self-reported contouring time, and perceived complexity of the cases. Results Between Sept 11, 2023, and Jan 20, 2025, 85 patients were enrolled; 83 were included in the analysis (41 control, 42 AI-assisted). The median difference in APL (AI-assisted minus control, negative favoring the intervention) was -0.02 [-0.32; 0.07] for GTV-T and 0.06 [-0.01; 0.14] for GTV-N. Conference duration, contouring time, and perceived complexity were similar between groups. No adverse events were reported. Conclusion The median difference in APL between groups was consistent with no relevant effect for GTV-T. For GTV-N, however, AI-assisted contouring tended towards more editing during peer review for APL, but not for supplementary contour metrics. No efficiency benefits were demonstrated. Overall, these findings do not indicate a concern, but warrants further research before widespread adoption.

title: Predictors of radiation-induced lymphopenia in NSCLC: blood and bone marrow dose during chemoradiotherapy.
abstract: Purpose Radiation-induced lymphopenia (RIL) is a significant complication for patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) undergoing radiotherapy, particularly as immunotherapy becomes increasingly integral to treatment. Understanding the predictors and mechanisms underlying RIL will support and help direct efforts to preserve anti-tumor immunity and optimizing therapeutic outcomes. Methods This study assessed the relationship between radiation dose to the blood and bone marrow and the development and recovery of lymphopenia in two (training and validation) cohorts, 134 patients in total, with NSCLC treated with either proton (PSPT) or photon-based chemoradiotherapy (CRT) between June 2009 and March 2014. Compartmental blood flow models and automatic organ segmentation were used to quantify radiation doses to circulating blood, large vessels and proliferating bone marrow. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify significant predictors of severe lymphopenia within 2 months from CRT start and its recovery. Results We found that both the generalized equivalent uniform dose (gEUD) to blood and baseline absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) were significant predictors of grade 4 lymphopenia. The discriminative ability (measured by AUC) for blood dose gEUD peaked around negative alpha values, suggesting that low-dose contributions to the blood pool are most relevant for predicting lymphopenia risk. Despite proton therapy delivering mean blood doses lower by 12.1% (p = 0.006) compared to photon therapy, there were no significant differences in nadir lymphocyte counts between the modalities. Bone marrow dose was only weakly correlated with lymphocyte nadir and showed no association with lymphocyte recovery after treatment. Conclusion Our findings demonstrate that radiation dose to circulating blood is a significant predictor of radiation-induced lymphopenia in NSCLC patients. Despite the observed correlations, these findings suggest that optimizing radiation dose to the blood alone may not be the most effective strategy for reducing lymphopenia.

title: Phase I dose-escalation study of stereotactic body radiotherapy with elective nodal irradiation for borderline resectable and unresectable locally advanced pancreatic cancer.
abstract: Background Locoregional recurrence remains a major clinical challenge in borderline resectable (BR) and unresectable locally advanced (UR-LA) pancreatic cancer, even after stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT). This phase I trial evaluated the safety, maximum tolerated dose (MTD), and preliminary efficacy of adding prophylactic elective nodal irradiation (ENI) to 5-fraction SBRT. Methods Patients with BR/UR-LAPC were enrolled in a 3 + 3 dose-escalation design. SBRT was delivered in 5 fractions using either adaptive magnetic resonance image-guided radiation therapy or respiratory breath-hold radiotherapy with a fiducial marker. The ENI dose was fixed at 30 Gy in five fractions, while the primary tumor dose increased from Level 1 (35 Gy) to Level 3 (40 Gy). The primary endpoint was acute dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) (any Grade ≥ 3 non-hematological adverse events within 14 days after the completion of SBRT). Results Twelve patients (BR: 4, LA: 8) were enrolled, 11 of whom had previously received systemic chemotherapy. One patient at Level 1 experienced acute Grade 3 anorexia/nausea requiring hospitalization. No DLTs were observed at Levels 2 and 3, and the MTD was not reached. Three patients with preexisting biliary stents developed subacute Grade 3 cholangitis. No Grade ≥ 3 late adverse events occurred. The median overall survival after SBRT was 17.3 months, and the 1-year locoregional control rate was 75%. Conclusion Five-fraction SBRT with simultaneous 30 Gy ENI was feasible, and the MTD was not reached within the tested dose levels up to 40 Gy. Further prospective studies are needed to evaluate its long-term safety and treatment outcomes.

title: Independent validation of a predictive risk model for contrast-enhancing brain lesions supports enhanced periventricular radiosensitivity and variable proton RBE.
abstract: Background and purpose Contrast-enhancing brain lesions (CEBLs) were reported as MR-imaging (MRI) endpoint to assess dose effects in healthy brain tissue following proton radiotherapy (PRT) of low-grade-glioma (LGG) patients. A voxel-level risk model was proposed with absorbed dose (D), dose-averaged linear energy transfer (LET D ), and proximity to the ventricular system as risk factors. We validated this model in an independent LGG patient cohort. Material and methods LGG patients treated at the same institution but more recently (2015-2019) were considered. For each patient, follow-up MRI data were screened for CEBLs, complication-risk maps were calculated and patient-level NTCP CEBL values were determined according to the original model. Eventually, risk model coefficients were updated by regressing the original logistic model to the validation cohort (validC) data. Results The validC comprised 112 subjects. Observed CEBL incidence of 21% was the same as in the modelling cohort (modelC); observed number of CEBLs and median lesion volume were considerably smaller in the validC, (N validC = 26, N modelC = 67 and V med,validC = 110 mm 3 , V med,modelC = 235 mm 3 ). Good calibration of the original patient-level NTCP CEBL model was obtained in the validC. Update of the model coefficients yielded a more pronounced LET D -effect and a 2.4 times higher odds ratio for the complication risk in the periventricular space (PVS). Conclusions The presented validation confirms an enhanced radiosensitivity of the PVS, a variable proton RBE, and supports serial complication characteristics of the brain. This underlines the need for a PRT strategy that actively spares the PVS under consideration of an LET D -dependent proton RBE. Clinical trial information The study was approved by the ethics committee of the Heidelberg University Hospital (ethics vote: S-516/2022).

title: Femoral artery Doppler, an innovative predictor of successful caudal block: A prospective observational study.
abstract: Background Caudal block is a common regional anaesthesia technique in paediatric surgery. Although various parameters have been proposed to evaluate the success of this block, the optimal, gold standard assessment method remains elusive. This study aims to examine the potential of femoral artery Doppler indices as a non-invasive, objective tool for predicting the efficacy of caudal block. Methods In this prospective observational study, 44 paediatric patients undergoing surgery under general anaesthesia with caudal block were assessed. Standard anaesthesia protocols were followed, and femoral artery Doppler ultrasound was performed at 3 time points: before the block, and 15 and 30 minutes after. Pulsatility index, resistive index, and waveform morphology were recorded. Changes in pulsatility index, resistive index, and morphology were analysed to predict block success. Results Caudal block was successful in 36 (82%) of the 44 patients. Significant reductions in pulsatility index and resistive index were observed in this group, with the change in pulsatility index showing the highest predictive accuracy (AUC = 1.00, sensitivity 97%, specificity 100%). ΔM also showed strong predictive value (AUCs of 0.95 and 0.97, respectively). Morphological changes from triphasic to monophasic waveforms were seen in 94% of successful blocks. Patients with successful blocks required less intraoperative fentanyl and had lower postoperative FLACC scores. Conclusion Femoral artery Doppler indices, particularly the change in pulsatility index, are a highly accurate and non-invasive predictor of successful caudal block in paediatric patients. Furthermore, alterations in Doppler waveform morphology showed a 100% positive predictive value in identifying block success, underscoring their potential as robust indicators in clinical practice.

title: 18 F-FDG PET-based radiomics for the prediction of aggressive/high-grade tumor in patients with cartilaginous tumors: A preliminary study.
abstract: Objective To assess the role of texture analysis of pre-treatment 18 F-FDG PET in the prediction of aggressive/high-grade tumor subtypes of cartilaginous tumors. Materials and methods Patients with cartilaginous tumors (benign cartilaginous tumors or CSs) who underwent pre-treatment 18 F-FDG PET for primary staging or restaging of recurrent disease were included in this retrospective study. Demographic and clinicopathologic data were collected. Textural and conventional PET parameters (maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax), SUVmean, metabolic tumor volume (MTV), and total lesion glycolysis (TLG)) were obtained from PET/CT images using LIFEx program. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression analysis was performed for feature selection. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to determine predictors of aggressive/high-grade tumor subtypes in cartilaginous tumors. Results A total of 29 18 F-FDG PET scans from 26 patients were included in the present study. Among 29 included 18 F-FDG PET scans, 18 (62.1%) scans were performed in patients with a benign/low-grade tumor(benign cartilaginous tumors and G1-2 CSs), while 11 (37.9%) scans were performed in patients with an aggressive/high-grade tumor(G3, dedifferentiated, mesenchymal, and other aggressive CSs). In the LASSO logistic regression analysis, seven potential predictors were selected for predicting aggressive/high-grade cartilaginous tumors. Whereas SUVmax (p = 0.025), SUVmean (p = 0.028), GLRLM_Run Entropy (p = 0.007), GLSZM_ZSE (p = 0.011), and GLSZM_SZLGLE (p = 0.007) were significantly associated with aggressive/high-grade pathology in univariate analysis, GLRLM_Run Entropy was found as the only independent predictor in multivariate analysis. Conclusion Tumor heterogeneity assessed by texture analysis of pre-treatment 18 F-FDG PET may be a significant predictor of aggressive/high-grade tumor subtypes in cartilaginous tumors.

title: Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms: Integrating WHO Classification with CT, MRI, and Molecular Imaging.
abstract: Pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (pNENs) are a heterogeneous group of tumors within gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (GEP-NENs), with variable clinical behavior and prognosis. The World Health Organization (WHO) classification distinguishes well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) from poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs), including the recognition of grade 3 NETs (NET G3) as a separate entity with important clinical implications. Multiphasic computed tomography (CT) and multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are central to detection, staging, and follow-up, with MRI offering superior sensitivity for liver metastases, particularly with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and hepatobiliary phase (HBP). Molecular imaging with somatostatin receptor-targeted PET and 18 F-FDG PET provides complementary biologic information by assessing receptor expression, metabolic aggressiveness, and tumor heterogeneity. SSTR-targeted PET supports confirmation of neuroendocrine phenotype, whole-body staging, and selection of candidates for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, whereas 18 F-FDG PET identifies aggressive or dedifferentiated tumor components that may influence prognosis and favor chemotherapy-oriented strategies. Despite advances, noninvasive grading remains limited, requiring integration of imaging with histopathology. An integrated multimodality approach combining CT, MRI, molecular imaging, and pathology is therefore essential for accurate staging, biopsy targeting, treatment stratification, and personalized management.

title: AI-driven radiopharmaceutical dosimetry optimization for theranostics: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Introduction Personalised radioligand therapy (RLT) depends on accurate absorbed-dose estimation. Standard dosimetry requires multiple post-therapy single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT) acquisitions, imposing logistical burdens. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have been proposed to streamline organ segmentation, generate synthetic imaging timepoints, and predict patient-specific doses. We evaluated the performance, methodological quality, and translational readiness of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven dosimetry in the clinical theranostics literature. Methods In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and regional databases (Jan 1, 2014, to March 1, 2025). Studies applying AI to dosimetry in human RLT recipients were eligible. Two reviewers screened and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed with the Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool (PROBAST) and the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2). Meta-analyses of organ segmentation (Dice similarity coefficient [DSC]) and dose prediction (concordance correlation coefficient [CCC]) used restricted maximum-likelihood (REML) random-effects models restricted to studies with independent validation sets. Prospero CRD420261349805 (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?RecordID=1349805). Results 58 studies met inclusion criteria covering 1847 patients (1523 [82%] male, 324 [18%] female). 23 studies with independent validation were eligible for meta-analysis. Pooled DSC was 0.87 (95% CI 0.83-0.90; 16 studies). Pooled voxel dosimetry relative absolute error (RAE) was 6.1% (4.6%-8.1%; 12 studies). Pretherapy kidney dose prediction yielded pooled CCC 0.79 (0.72-0.85; 8 studies). PROBAST identified high risk of bias in 71% of prediction studies. Reducing timepoints from ≥3 to 1-2 scans increased RAE by 8.2 percentage points (5.1-11.4). AI reduced median processing time from 180 to 25 min. Conclusions On independent validation data, AI-driven dosimetry shows promising accuracy for organ-level dose estimation and substantially reduces processing time. However, the evidence base remains immature: 71% of prediction studies carry high risk of bias, only four studies report external validation, and most pooled outcomes were graded as low or very low certainty. External multicentre validation and prospective randomised trials comparing AI-guided against fixed-activity RLT are needed before clinical adoption. Current evidence primarily demonstrates technical feasibility rather than proven clinical utility.

title: Clinical significance of the COPD assessment test in evaluating treatment response in Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease.
abstract: Background In Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease (MAC-PD), sputum culture conversion is a key endpoint but does not fully reflect symptom burden. We evaluated the COPD Assessment Test (CAT) as a patient-reported measure of disease severity and treatment response. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 179 treatment episodes in 174 patients with MAC-PD who continued therapy for at least 12 months. CAT scores were assessed at baseline and at 6 and 12 months. We examined associations of baseline CAT scores with chest computed tomography (CT) scores and sputum culture status, and of CAT changes (Δ6 and Δ12) with the 12-month culture-positive versus culture-negative/sputum-unobtainable classification and a study-defined composite incorporating 12-month radiographic response and the microbiologic course through 24 months. Results Baseline CAT scores correlated weakly with CT scores and were higher in baseline culture-positive and poorly controlled episodes. Neither Δ6 nor Δ12 differed by 12-month culture classification. Δ12 was more favorable in well-controlled than in poorly controlled episodes (p = 0.010), but discrimination was limited (area under the curve, 0.646 in all classifiable episodes and 0.682 in those with baseline CAT > 2). In the latter subgroup, an exploratory decrease of at least 3 points showed a sensitivity of 52.0% and a specificity of 71.9%. Conclusions CAT may complement microbiologic and radiographic assessments by capturing patient-reported symptom changes. The limited discriminatory performance does not support the use of CAT alone to classify treatment control.

title: French protocol for the diagnosis and management of chronic nonbacterial osteomyelitis.
abstract: Chronic Nonbacterial Osteomyelitis (CNO) is a primary, non-infectious inflammatory bone disorder predominantly affecting children (median age 10 years), with a female predominance. It presents as bone pain with an inflammatory pattern, sometimes accompanied by localised swelling, and follows a relapsing-remitting course. Typical lesions involve the metaphysis of the lower limbs, while clavicular, mandibular, and vertebral involvement may also occur, the latter often being asymptomatic. Cutaneous manifestations (such as palmoplantar pustulosis), articular features, or gut inflammation may coexist, placing the disease within the broader spectrum of Synovitis, Acne, Pustulosis, Hyperostosis, and Osteitis (SAPHO) syndrome. Diagnosis is based on imaging, with whole-body MRI being the gold standard in children. It reveals multiple, symmetric inflammatory bone lesions often exceeding the clinically apparent sites. Bone biopsy is reserved for atypical or unifocal presentations or when a diagnostic uncertainty persists. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are the first-line treatment. In refractory cases or in patients with vertebral involvement, second-line therapies - including intravenous bisphosphonates or TNF inhibitors - may be considered off-label. Management primarily aims to control pain and preserve quality of life. Overall prognosis is favourable, with spontaneous remission in most patients after a median disease duration of four years. However, up to 50% of patients still experience flares after five years, and orthopaedic sequelae or spinal deformities may persist. General practitioners play a key role in early recognition, appropriate referral to specialist care, avoidance of unnecessary bone biopsies, and initial therapeutic management.

title: Cost-utility and cost-effectiveness of COPD screening as an add-on to low dose computed tomography lung cancer screening in Germany.
abstract: Background COPD is associated with high disease burden and is a leading cause of death. In July 2024, Germany introduced regulation allowing low-dose CT for early lung cancer detection in smokers. This cost-utility and cost-effectiveness model compares hypothetical lung cancer screening with embedded COPD screening (LC+COPD screening) with lung cancer screening alone (LC-screening). Methods A dynamic Markov model from the perspective of the statutory health insurance was developed including individuals aged 50-75 years meeting current German lung cancer screening criteria. The base-case assumed a smoking cessation success rate of 12% among individuals with newly detected COPD compared to 7.5% among individuals with known and undetected COPD. The model used a 40-year time horizon with 3-month cycles. Outcomes include costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) and life years gained (LYG). Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted. Results Under base-case assumptions, the ICER was €59,868 per QALY gained and €32,175 per LYG. Assuming an increased smoking cessation success rate of 15% among individuals with newly detected COPD, ICERs were €35,349 per QALY gained and €17,967 per LYG. Univariate sensitivity analyses showed the greatest impact from discount rates and smoking cessation success. Probabilistic sensitivity analyses with 10,000 draws each yielded mean ICERs of €59,038 per QALY gained and €31,821 per LYG. Discussion Our model provides a first indication of the cost-effectiveness of LC+COPD-screening. The findings are limited by, among other things, lack of knowledge about the utilization of services for undiagnosed COPD and assumptions about the utilization and success of smoking cessation measures.

title: [Unfavorable prognosis of pathogenic variants in the telomerase complex in cases of familial pulmonary fibrosis].
abstract: Introduction Pathogenic variants located in genes involved in telomere homeostasis (telomere-related genes [TRGs]) are associated with cases of familial pulmonary fibrosis (FPF). The aim of our study was to characterize the clinical presentation and prognosis of patients with FPF according to the presence or absence of a pathogenic variant involving a TRG. Methods We conducted a retrospective, observational, single-center study including all patients with FPF followed at the Rare Lung Diseases Reference Center of Bichat-Claude-Bernard Hospital (Paris, France) and analyzed between 2021 and 2024, using next-generation sequencing of a single 30-gene panel associated with FPF. Results Fifty-six patients were included. Median age at diagnosis of interstitial lung disease (ILD) was 65 years. Thirty-three patients (59%) exhibited a CT pattern of usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP), four (7%) had a nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) pattern, and three (5%) displayed a bronchiolocentric interstitial pneumonia pattern. The diagnoses retained after multidisciplinary discussion (MDD) were as follows: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis in 29 patients (52%), hypersensitivity pneumonitis in four (7%), ILD associated with rheumatoid arthritis in four (7%), and idiopathic NSIP in three (5%). A pathogenic TRG variant was detected in 12 patients (21%): TERT (n=4), PARN (n=4), RTEL1 (n=3), and TERC (n=1). The frequency of pulmonary and extrapulmonary manifestations at diagnosis did not differ significantly between patients with or without a pathogenic TRG variant. Patients carrying a pathogenic TRG variant underwent more rapid annual decline in forced vital capacity (-4.54 vs. -1.75 percentage points; P=0.044). Conclusion These results confirm the unfavorable prognostic impact of an identified pathogenic variant of a TRG in patients with FPF, which is associated with a particularly rapid decline in respiratory function.

title: MRI-based volume assessments show no changes in hippocampus, amygdala, thalamus and brainstem subregions in narcolepsy type 1.
abstract: Study objectives Narcolepsy type 1 (NT1) is characterized by excessive daytime sleepiness and cataplexy. Previous studies have implicated the amygdala, thalamus, brainstem and hippocampus in the pathophysiology of NT1. We here aimed to examine more detailed subregional case-control differences in MRI-based segmentations of these brain regions to gain deeper insights. Methods We obtained 3T MRI brain scans from 54 NT1 patients (39 females, mean age 21.8 ± 11.0 years, 51 with confirmed hypocretin-deficiency and three patients that had not performed this measure) and 114 healthy controls (77 females, mean age 23.2 ± 9.0 years). Automated segmentation of the hippocampus, amygdala, thalamus, and brainstem was performed on T1-weighted MRI data using FreeSurfer. Case-control volume differences were tested using general linear models and permutation testing. The false discovery rate was controlled at 5 % with the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. Results The analysis revealed no significant case-control differences for any of the subregions in the hippocampus, thalamus, amygdala and brainstem after correction for multiple testing. Conclusions Based on a detailed automated MRI-based segmentation analyses in a relatively large national sample, NT1 patients had no significant changes in any amygdala, thalamus, brainstem or hippocampus subregions compared to controls. In the future large multi-site studies could be performed to achieve sufficient power to detect more subtle group differences.

title: Radiation in Spine Care: A Comprehensive Review of Radiation Sources, Emerging Technology, Cancer Risk, and Radiation Stewardship.
abstract: Radiation from medical imaging is increasingly recognized as a modifiable carcinogenic exposure. The precise population-level cancer burden remains debated, but the oncologic cost is real, unevenly distributed by patient age and sex and largely controllable at the point of clinical decision-making. Spine care occupies a central position in this discussion because many patients are exposed to ionizing radiation repeatedly over the course of their care. This includes patients within a wide age range undergoing surgery, fluoroscopic- or computerized tomography (CT)-guided percutaneous interventions, and serial imaging. In younger patients, the attributable cancer risk per unit dose is greater and the latency period for radiation-induced malignancy is longer; in patients requiring repeated interventions, cumulative lifetime radiation exposure may also become substantial. These concerns are increasingly relevant as navigation, robotics, and augmented reality platforms have expanded the use of preoperative and intraoperative CT. In this context, we sought to synthesize the current evidence across radiation physics, carcinogenesis risk modeling, perioperative radiation sources, patient-level risk heterogeneity, surgeon and operating room personnel exposure, and technology-specific evidence. Particular attention is paid to patient-level heterogeneity as cancer risk per unit dose varies by nearly an order of magnitude across age and sex strata such that oncologic implications of an otherwise identical imaging protocol may differ substantially depending on the patient receiving it. Building on the evidence, we introduce a radiation budgeting framework that treats the full perioperative episode as the unit of radiation accountability and propose radiation stewardship in spine care as a structural analog to antibiotic stewardship in infectious disease.

title: Arthroscopically assisted lower trapezius transfer with semitendinosus autograft in massive rotator cuff tears: a prospective study.
abstract: Purpose The optimal management of massive rotator cuff tears associated with absence of external rotation remains unclear. The present study reports the clinical results in patients managed arthroscopically with lower trapezius transfers augmented with free autologous semitendinosus tendon alone or in combination with superior capsular reconstruction with up to 2 years follow-up. Methods Patients treated from May 2019 to July 2024 were enrolled prospectively. Inclusion criteria were pain, inability to elevate and rotate externally the affected shoulder. Preoperative shoulder radiographs and magnetic resonance imaging were collected. Clinical assessment and range of motion evaluation was performed using the VAS, CS, and ASES at 3 and 6 months, at 1- and 2-years follow-up. Shoulder radiographs and magnetic resonance imaging were performed at 6 months and 2 year follow-up. Results None of the 35 patients originally enrolled was lost at follow-up. In 18 of 35 shoulders, a superior capsular reconstruction using the LHBT was performed. The baseline Constant score was 32 (±16), the American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons Shoulder Score was 15 (±9.5) and VAS at baseline was 6 (±2.9). At final follow-up, they improved to 66 (±15.4), 82 (±7.4) and 1 (±1.1), respectively. Range of motion increased from a mean of 90° for forward flexion, from 50° for abduction, and from 0° for external rotation to a mean of 140°, 100° and 48°, respectively. All patients showed statistically significant improvement for all scores and movements, especially external rotation (p < 0.05), at 3 and 6 months. Conclusions Arthroscopic lower trapezius transfer with autologous semitendinosus augmentation in patients with massive rotator cuff tears with limited or absent external rotation is safe and effective, with predictable pain relief and good clinical outcomes.

title: Fluid fluctuation and visual outcomes in neovascular age-related macular degeneration: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Fluctuation in retinal thickness and fluid during anti-vascular endothelial growrh factor (VEGF) therapy has emerged as a candidate prognostic biomarker in neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), but the evidence is heterogeneous and has not been quantitatively synthesized. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to December, 2025, for studies reporting retinal fluid or thickness fluctuation metrics and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) outcomes in eyes receiving anti-VEGF therapy for nAMD, including both observational studies and post hoc analyses of randomized trials. Between-group mean differences (MDs) in BCVA change were pooled using random-effects models, stratified by study design and optical coherence tomography parameter, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Seventeen studies comprising 19 reports and 9873 eyes were included. Among observ ational studies at 24 months, eyes in the highest fluctuation category had significantly smaller BCVA gains than those in the lowest for every parameter examined: intraretinal fluid (MD -7.00 letters, 95% CI -10.27 to -3.72), subretinal fluid (-5.02, -8.09 to -1.95), pigment epithelial detachment (-8.41, -14.54 to -2.27), total fluid (-9.42, -12.69 to -6.15), and central subfield thickness (-10.56, -14.40 to -6.73), with low to moderate heterogeneity (I² 0-42.6%). Among post hoc analyses of randomized trials at 24 months, the pooled difference was -6.02 letters (-8.72 to -3.32), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 77.2%) that leave-one-out analysis showed did not alter the direction or significance of the estimate. Greater fluctuation was additionally associated with approximately twice the odds of macular fibrosis and atrophy. Certainty of evidence was low to very low for most fluid compartments, limited principally by the non-randomized nature of the exposure and by the absence of a standardized definition of fluctuation across studies. Temporal anatomical stability, rather than the presence of fluid at any single visit, may therefore carry prognostic information beyond conventional measures of disease activity, though prospective evaluation using a common metric is required before stability can be adopted as a treatment target.

title: Late-onset filtering bleb complications: A review.
abstract: Late-onset filtering bleb dysfunction remains an important determinant of long-term outcomes following glaucoma filtration surgery. Although trabeculectomy provides sustained intraocular pressure (IOP) reduction, progressive changes in bleb architecture and wound healing can result in filtration failure, hypotony, leakage, ocular discomfort, and sight-threatening infection. We examine the clinical characteristics, underlying mechanisms, assessment, prevention, and management of late-onset bleb complications, with emphasis on individualized, mechanism-directed care. Standardized bleb grading systems facilitate documentation of morphology and longitudinal assessment. Anterior segment optical coherence tomography and ultrasound biomicroscopy complement clinical examination by delineating bleb architecture and identifying potential sites of outflow obstruction, while optical coherence tomography angiography offers an evolving approach to evaluating bleb vascularity. Elevated IOP may arise from internal ostial obstruction, scleral flap adhesion, subconjunctival fibrosis, or encapsulation. Management depends on the site and extent of dysfunction and includes medical therapy, laser intervention, antifibrotic-augmented needling, and surgical revision. Conversely, excessive filtration and compromised conjunctival integrity may cause persistent hypotony, bleb leakage, and hypotony-related structural changes. Treatment ranges from selected conservative measures to compression sutures, conjunctival advancement, and tissue grafting, according to the underlying defect and associated complications. Bleb-related infection requires urgent recognition and treatment, with management determined by the extent of intraocular involvement. Related complications following glaucoma drainage device implantation, nonpenetrating surgery, and subconjunctival microstent procedures are also considered. Successful long-term care requires balancing adequate aqueous drainage against the risks of overfiltration, tissue fragility, and infection. Lifelong surveillance, patient education, and timely intervention remain central to preserving visual function. Future advances in quantitative imaging, targeted wound modulation, and safer filtration strategies may improve the durability and safety of bleb-dependent glaucoma surgery.

title: Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment: A Contemporary Review of Repair Techniques, Common Complications, Advances in Imaging and Access to Care.
abstract: Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) is a vision-threatening ophthalmic emergency with a rising global incidence driven by aging populations and the worldwide myopia epidemic. Despite modern surgical techniques achieving anatomic reattachment in over 90% of cases, as many as 40% of successfully reattached eyes fail to recover functional vision, underscoring a persistent and clinically important gap between anatomic and visual outcomes. We synthesize contemporary evidence across a wide clinical spectrum of RRD. We examine the pathophysiologic cascade initiated by posterior vitreous detachment, the classification and clinical significance of types of retinal breaks, and the epidemiologic burden of established risk factors including high myopia, pseudophakia, and hereditary vitreoretinal disorders. The historical evolution of repair techniques is reviewed. Evidence based rationale for personalized surgical selection in phakic, pseudophakic, and giant retinal tear-associated detachments is then discussed. The most common complications of surgical repair are addressed, with particular emphasis on proliferative vitreoretinopathy as the dominant cause of surgical failure and the most pressing unmet therapeutic need. We further examine how neighborhood-level social determinants of health independently shape presentation severity and visual recovery, underscoring that equitable access to timely care can be as fundamental to influencing outcomes as surgical technique itself. Finally, emerging pharmacologic strategies, intraoperative optical coherence tomography, robotic surgical assistance, and imaging prognostic tools, with and without the use of artificial intelligence are evaluated as future directions. Advancing outcomes in RRD will require the integration of surgical refinement, emerging pharmacology, imaging-based prognostication, and an unwavering commitment to equitable access across all patient populations.

title: Retinal deposits: A narrative review of genetic causes and their phenocopies.
abstract: Retinal deposits represent a structurally convergent but biologically heterogeneous manifestation of numerous inherited retinal diseases and frequently pose a diagnostic challenge because similar funduscopic phenotypes may arise from distinct genetic and molecular mechanisms. We performed a structured narrative review of the literature to synthesize the genetic causes of subretinal, sub-retinal pigment epithelium, and intraretinal deposit phenotypes, with emphasis on molecular pathophysiology, anatomical localization on optical coherence tomography, characteristic imaging features, and natural history. Across disease groups, deposits were found to result from diverse mechanisms, including visual cycle dysfunction, impaired photoreceptor outer segment processing, extracellular matrix and Bruch membrane abnormalities, lipid metabolic defects, and crystalline metabolite accumulation. Despite overlapping clinical appearances such as vitelliform material, flecks, drusen-like lesions, or crystalline deposits, optical coherence tomography allows consistent compartmental classification relative to the retinal pigment epithelium, which in turn correlates with underlying biology and genotype. Visual cycle-related flecked retina disorders demonstrate progressive rod dysfunction distinct from stationary phenotypes, while sub-retinal pigment epithelium deposits in monogenic macular dystrophies may mimic age-related macular degeneration, but differ in age of onset, inheritance pattern, and complication risk. Recognition of these genotype-deposit correlations and application of a compartment-based classification may improve differential diagnosis; guide targeted genetic testing and support the development of imaging biomarkers relevant to emerging gene-directed therapies.

title: Pharmacogenomic testing and survival in oesophageal cancer patients, a literature review and results from selected SNPs in the UK MRC OE02 trial.
abstract: Background Germline single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) are biomarkers that can be readily measured using DNA from peripheral blood or normal tissue. While SNPs have been associated with survival and cytotoxic chemotherapy response in several cancers, limited data exist on the clinical relevance of selected SNPs in oesophageal cancer (OeC) patients. Methods DNA was extracted from normal tissue of 480 OeC patients treated with either surgery alone (S, n = 233) or chemotherapy followed by surgery (CS, n = 247) in the OE02 trial. SNPs in DPYD, OPRT, ERCC1, ERCC2 and XRCC1, GSTP1 and TS were analysed using MassARRAY, Sanger sequencing or gel electrophoresis. Associations with clinicopathological variables and overall survival (OS) were investigated. Results Selected SNP variants were associated with age, tumour differentiation, tumour regression and OS. The OPRT rs1801019 'GC' genotype was more frequent in patients aged >65 years (p = 0.034); the TS 5'UTR '3R/3R' genotype was more frequent in poorly differentiated tumours (p = 0.019) and the ERCC2 rs13181 'GG' genotype was nominally associated with improved tumour regression (p = 0.041). In an exploratory analysis, the ERCC1 rs11615 'CT' genotype was associated with improved OS (HR 0.80, 95%CI: 0.65-0.99, p = 0.040) in the whole cohort and in the subgroup of patients with adenocarcinoma treated by surgery alone. No associations were observed for any of the other SNPs. Conclusion In the largest germline SNP analysis in OeC to date, ERCC1 rs11615 'CT' emerged as a candidate prognostic biomarker warranting validation in an independent cohort.

title: Whole-tumor dual-layer spectral detector CT quantification for preoperative identification of poorly differentiated cervical squamous cell carcinoma: An interpretable prediction model.
abstract: Objectives To develop an interpretable dual-layer spectral detector CT (DLCT) model for preoperative identification of poorly differentiated cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC), and to compare two-dimensional region-of-interest (2D ROI) with whole-tumor three-dimensional volume-of-interest (3D VOI) parameter-extraction strategies. Methods This retrospective study included 205 surgically treated patients with CSCC who underwent contrast-enhanced DLCT before surgery. Patients were assigned to training (n = 113), internal validation (n = 47), and temporal validation (n = 45) cohorts. Parameters were extracted using 2D ROI- and 3D VOI-based analyses. Clinical, 2D DLCT, 3D DLCT, and DLCT-clinical fusion models were developed using multivariable logistic regression and evaluated by discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Results 3D VOI-based analysis showed higher interobserver reproducibility than 2D ROI-based analysis (mean intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.950 vs. 0.875; P < 0.001). The 3D DLCT model included arterial-phase 70-keV virtual monoenergetic attenuation (CT 70keV-AP ), arterial-phase normalized effective atomic number (NZeff AP ), and venous-phase normalized iodine density (NID VP ). Its areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.897, 0.895, and 0.885 in the training, internal validation, and temporal validation cohorts, respectively. The 2D DLCT and 3D DLCT models did not differ significantly in AUCs after multiple-comparison correction. The fusion model achieved AUCs of 0.900, 0.916, and 0.881, respectively, outperforming the clinical model without significantly improving on the 3D DLCT model. Conclusions 3D DLCT quantification provides an interpretable and noninvasive imaging biomarker for preoperative identification of poorly differentiated CSCC and may support individualized risk stratification. External validation in larger multicenter cohorts is needed to confirm generalizability.

title: Survival predictors in unresectable stage III NSCLC treated with induction chemoimmunotherapy: a real-world multicenter study of treatment cycles, response, and maintenance duration.
abstract: Background Optimal integration of induction chemoimmunotherapy with definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) and maintenance immunotherapy for unresectable stage III NSCLC remains undefined. Methods This multicenter retrospective study included 321 patients who received induction chemoimmunotherapy followed by CRT with or without maintenance immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Landmark survival from radiotherapy completion was used to avoid guarantee-time bias. Results Patients receiving 1-2 induction cycles showed numerically longer median PFS (28.0 months) than those with 3-4 (24.6) or >4 cycles (14.2; log-rank p = 0.179), but this trend was confounded by higher concurrent CRT rates in the 1-2 cycle group (74.5%vs. 47.1% vs. 33.7%). After propensity-score matching, the response-related survival advantage was attenuated (HR for PFS 0.70, p = 0.079). In matched analyses, maintenance ICI was associated with improved PFS (25.2 vs. 8.9 months; HR 0.47) and OS (NR vs. 22.0 months; HR 0.24) (both p < 0.001). An exploratory data-driven analysis suggested that >9 maintenance cycles yielded further PFS (HR 0.23) and OS (HR 0.17) benefits. Conclusion In this real-world cohort, induction cycle number did not significantly affect survival; the apparent advantage of 1-2 cycles was likely confounded. Early radiographic response was not an independent predictor after matching. Maintenance ICI was associated with improved outcomes, and >9 cycles showed additional benefit, though with potential bias. These findings provide hypotheses for prospective trial design.

title: Multiomics pan‑cancer analysis identifies CA9 as an immunosuppression‑linked prognostic biomarker: Validation of oncogenic and radiomic‑based predictive value in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Carbonic anhydrase IX (CA9) is a tumor-associated transmembrane metalloenzyme implicated in tumor progression, yet its pan-cancer roles and biomarker potential remain underexplored. In this study, we performed the comprehensive and systematic pan-cancer multi-omics analysis of CA9 using data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and multiple analytical platforms, and further validated its functional significance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) through cellular experiments. A radiomics model was also constructed from CT imaging data to predict CA9 expression and prognosis in HCC. Our results showed that CA9 mRNA was significantly upregulated in most cancers and associated with poor prognosis. High CA9 expression correlated with tumor mutation burden, microsatellite instability, tumor heterogeneity, immune cell infiltration, and immune checkpoint molecules. Single-cell data revealed predominant CA9 expression in malignant cells, and pathway enrichment suggested an association between CA9 expression and HIF-1, PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling, and efferocytosis pathways. Functional experiments confirmed that CA9 promotes HCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. Collectively, CA9 shows potential as a pan-cancer diagnostic and prognostic biomarker and is associated with immune-related features, with a possible role in HCC progression. The radiomics model offers a non-invasive approach for predicting CA9 expression.

title: DCE-MRI muscle perfusion changes after stem cell transplantation for diabetic lower extremity arterial disease: Association with clinical ischemic improvement.
abstract: Objective To investigate the value of dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) in assessing the early muscle perfusion response to autologous peripheral blood stem cell transplantation (PBSCT) in diabetic lower extremity arteriosclerosis obliterans (DLASO), and to analyze the relationship between imaging changes and improvement in clinical ischemia. Methods We retrospectively included 32 patients with DLASO who underwent PBSCT between April 2022 and April 2025, and compared the peak signal intensity (SI_peak) of the medial gastrocnemius, lateral gastrocnemius, and soleus, together with the gastrocnemius volume transfer constant (K trans ), rate constant (Kep), and extravascular extracellular volume fraction (Ve), before treatment and on day 3 after treatment; pain grade and intermittent claudication distance were evaluated during the same period. Changes before and after treatment were analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model, paired t test, or Wilcoxon signed-rank test, while Spearman correlation analysis and Cohen's κ test were used to examine the association and directional concordance between changes in K trans and clinical improvement. Results SI_peak increased after treatment in all three muscle groups, with P < 0.001 for each comparison after Holm correction; K trans , Kep, and Ve also increased (P < 0.001); among the 32 patients, pain grade decreased in 23 (71.88%) (Z = -4.290, P < 0.001). Among the 28 patients with complete walking data, intermittent claudication distance increased from 90.00 (60.00, 126.00) m to 115.00 (84.00, 153.00) m (P = 0.002). ΔK trans was positively correlated with the grade of pain improvement (ρ=0.440, P = 0.012) and with the change in intermittent claudication distance (ρ=0.491, P = 0.008); the directional concordance rates between the imaging response and the two clinical responses were 81.25% and 78.57%, respectively. Conclusion Early after PBSCT, DCE-MRI perfusion parameters of the calf muscles changed and showed moderate associations with improvements in pain and walking function; DCE-MRI may therefore serve as a quantitative imaging adjunct for assessing the early treatment response in DLASO.
originalAbstract:
Objective

To investigate the value of dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) in assessing the early muscle perfusion response to autologous peripheral blood stem cell transplantation (PBSCT) in diabetic lower extremity arteriosclerosis obliterans (DLASO), and to analyze the relationship between imaging changes and improvement in clinical ischemia.

Methods

We retrospectively included 32 patients with DLASO who underwent PBSCT between April 2022 and April 2025, and compared the peak signal intensity (SI_peak) of the medial gastrocnemius, lateral gastrocnemius, and soleus, together with the gastrocnemius volume transfer constant (Ktrans), rate constant (Kep), and extravascular extracellular volume fraction (Ve), before treatment and on day 3 after treatment; pain grade and intermittent claudication distance were evaluated during the same period. Changes before and after treatment were analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model, paired t test, or Wilcoxon signed-rank test, while Spearman correlation analysis and Cohen's κ test were used to examine the association and directional concordance between changes in Ktrans and clinical improvement.

Results

SI_peak increased after treatment in all three muscle groups, with P < 0.001 for each comparison after Holm correction; Ktrans, Kep, and Ve also increased (P < 0.001); among the 32 patients, pain grade decreased in 23 (71.88%) (Z = -4.290, P < 0.001). Among the 28 patients with complete walking data, intermittent claudication distance increased from 90.00 (60.00, 126.00) m to 115.00 (84.00, 153.00) m (P = 0.002). ΔKtrans was positively correlated with the grade of pain improvement (ρ=0.440, P = 0.012) and with the change in intermittent claudication distance (ρ=0.491, P = 0.008); the directional concordance rates between the imaging response and the two clinical responses were 81.25% and 78.57%, respectively.

Conclusion

Early after PBSCT, DCE-MRI perfusion parameters of the calf muscles changed and showed moderate associations with improvements in pain and walking function; DCE-MRI may therefore serve as a quantitative imaging adjunct for assessing the early treatment response in DLASO.

title: Computed tomography extracellular volume fraction in canine hepatic fibrosis: a retrospective preliminary study.
abstract: Liver biopsy remains the gold standard for diagnosing hepatic fibrosis in dogs; however, its invasive nature limits suitability for repeated assessment. Computed tomography-extracellular volume fraction (CT-ECV) has been investigated as a quantitative imaging measure associated with hepatic fibrosis in humans; however, its characteristics in dogs with spontaneous hepatic fibrosis remain incompletely understood. This retrospective study aimed to compare hepatic CT-ECV between dogs with only histopathologically normal biopsied hepatic lobes and dogs with at least one biopsied hepatic lobe showing clinically significant fibrosis, and to explore the ability of CT-ECV to discriminate between these groups. Thirty-six client-owned dogs that underwent triple-phase contrast-enhanced CT and liver biopsy were analyzed. Histopathologic examination identified 47 histopathologically normal hepatic lobes from 26 dogs and 27 hepatic lobes with fibrosis from 11 dogs; one dog contributed hepatic lobes to both categories. CT-ECV was calculated from changes in hepatic and aortic attenuation between pre-contrast and equilibrium phase images, with correction for hematocrit. For the principal doglevel analysis, 25 dogs were classified as normal and 11 as fibrotic, and dog-level CTECV was calculated as the mean across all biopsied hepatic lobes. Mean dog-level CT-ECV was 21.46 ± 3.02% in the normal group and 32.75 ± 10.67% in the fibrosis group. After adjustment for CT scanner, CT-ECV was significantly higher in the fibrosis group, with an estimated mean difference of 12.10 percentage points (robust 95% CI, 4.60-19.59; P =.002). Dog-level receiver operating characteristic analysis yielded an area under the curve of 0.865 (95% CI, 0.726-1.000). An exploratory candidate threshold of 29.56% provided a sensitivity of 63.6% (95% CI, 30.8-89.1%) and a specificity of 100% (95% CI, 86.3-100%). Intra-observer repeatability was high (intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.886). These findings provide preliminary evidence that CT-ECV is associated with clinically significant hepatic fibrosis in dogs. Further studies using standardized imaging protocols and independent clinical populations are required to validate its diagnostic performance and the proposed exploratory threshold.

title: Dual-domain transformer low-frequency waveform recovery for quantitative ultrasound bone imaging.
abstract: Full-waveform inversion (FWI) of bone is highly susceptible to cycle skipping when bandwidth-limited ultrasound measurements lack reliable low-frequency information. To address this limitation, this study proposes a Dual-Domain Transformer Low-Frequency Recovery (DT-LFR) framework that recovers missing low-frequency waveforms from bandwidth-limited high-frequency observations by integrating time- and frequency-domain representations with window-based self-attention. The recovered waveforms are used in an initial low-frequency FWI stage to construct a large-scale background model for subsequent higher-frequency inversion. In numerical Models I and II, DT-LFR-guided FWI reduced the velocity RMSE by 87.87% and 77.98%, respectively, and the density RMSE by 45.45% and 38.66%, respectively, relative to inversion with insufficient low-frequency information. For the ex vivo tubular bone data, the reconstructed outer-contour Dice coefficient increased from 0.89 to 0.95, while the average symmetric surface distance decreased from 5.91 to 2.84 pixels. These results demonstrate that DT-LFR-derived low-frequency information can improve FWI initialization, thereby enhancing the stability and reconstruction accuracy of subsequent bone FWI under bandwidth-limited ultrasound acquisition.

title: Image-processing-based detection of defective ultrasound transducer elements using clinical B-mode images.
abstract: The use of medical ultrasound is critical in healthcare, with applications ranging from medical diagnosis to therapeutic procedures. The elements of the ultrasound transducer are the core of this technology, and over time, they degrade and fail. Current maintenance practices rely on periodic maintenance, making them inefficient due to extended intervals between evaluations, which may lead to damaged transducers remaining in operation since visual identification of the defect is infeasible. This study presents a method that uses images collected by a transducer during normal workflow to determine a probe's status. Firstly, histogram equalization and frame averaging were applied to the images to reduce variability across clinical images while reinforcing consistent artifact patterns produced by inactive elements. The output then underwent a feature-extraction stage involving denoising and vertical edge filtering. To further distinguish the artifacts from the background, Otsu thresholding and morphological processing were done on the resulting image. Subsequently, component analysis based on geometric and spatial positioning was conducted to isolate true defects from residual noise. The identified feature was then overlaid on the original averaged input image to indicate the location of the artifacts. System validation was performed using linear B-mode images from of porcine subjects across different anatomical regions to simulate the variability encountered in clinical settings. The technique used a column-strength profile derived from Sobel-filtered images, in which artifacts produced threshold values greater than 1, unlike artifact-free regions. Reliable artifact detection was achieved by averaging more than 50 images, resulting in a precise accuracy across all element conditions.

title: Erythrocyte radial fluctuations based ultrafast ultrasound Doppler imaging.
abstract: Ultrafast ultrasound Doppler has shown great enhancement of sensitivity to small blood flows. However, it reconstructs blood vessels by directly integrating blood flow signals, neglecting the variations of red blood cells backscattering properties, which may compromise spatial resolution. In this study, we consider this variation of point spread function (PSF) of blood flow speckle patterns. By strategically reducing the size of blood flow speckle patterns, we mitigate this variability, enabling enhanced spatial resolution. We integrate super-resolution radial fluctuation (SRRF) principles with contrast-free ultrafast ultrasound Doppler, terming SRRF-Doppler. SRRF-Doppler employs a gradient convergence-based operator to narrow blood flow speckle size. Unlike direct integration of blood flow signals, SRRF-Doppler leverages the temporal fluctuations in blood flow through higher-order statistical analysis to reconstruct vascular images. In addition, to address the challenge of dense blood flow speckle concentration, Fourier-based velocity separation filters are integrated into the SRRF-Doppler. The performance of SRRF-Doppler has been validated in simulations and in vivo datasets. Field II simulations measured that the spatial resolution reached 66 μm in the axial direction and 70 μm in the lateral direction (wavelength = 98.56 µm), and in vivo experiments demonstrated a two-fold enhancement in spatial resolution compared to ultrafast ultrasound Doppler. Furthermore, we validated the efficacy of SRRF-Doppler for functional neurovascular imaging through whisker stimulation experiments in awake rats. The preliminary clinical feasibility of SRRF-Doppler imaging was demonstrated by imaging results of human brain and intraspinal tumor.

title: Mean-shift-based spatiotemporal microbubble signal enhancement for high-concentration ultrasound localization microscopy.
abstract: Ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) achieves super-resolution microvascular imaging by localizing and tracking intravascular microbubbles. Under high-concentration conditions, echoes from adjacent microbubbles can overlap spatially, causing responses to broaden or merge and weakening the local peak structures required for conventional localization. Consequently, microbubble information already present in each frame may become difficult to detect and localize. We propose MS-ULM, a mean-shift-based pre-localization enhancement framework that improves the local peak representation of clutter-filtered microbubble signals so that conventional localization methods can recover more useful microbubble events for limited-frame reconstruction. MS-ULM uses mean-shift spatial aggregation to exploit local spatial-intensity distributions and concentrate spatially diffuse, overlapping, or low-saliency responses toward dominant local intensity peaks. Rather than explicitly separating every overlapping microbubble, it re-expresses existing microbubble information to better match the local peak structure required by conventional localization. Doppler-frequency-polarity-based directional separation and lag-1 temporal coherence processing are further incorporated to reduce directional mixing and suppress temporally incoherent fluctuations and isolated pseudo-peaks. The enhanced signals are processed using the same radial-symmetry localization, tracking, filtering, and reconstruction procedures as the baseline pipeline. Simulations showed improved recall and F1-score and greater retention of true-positive localizations in valid trajectories. In vivo rat brain experiments showed more valid trajectories, improved limited-frame vascular filling, and a Fourier ring correlation (FRC) resolution of 42.3±0.4μm; representative rat kidney experiments further supported cross-organ applicability. These results show that improving the pre-localization representation of existing microbubble information enables more complete high-concentration, limited-frame ULM reconstruction without modifying downstream algorithms.

title: Speed-of-sound validation in ring array ultrasound computed tomography using transmission-mode tissue-mimicking phantoms.
abstract: Ultrasound computed tomography (USCT) is a promising radiation-free quantitative imaging technique for soft tissue characterization, yet the absence of standardized validation phantoms hinders its clinical standardization and algorithm benchmarking. In this study, a suite of agar-based tissue-mimicking phantoms was developed and fabricated for the speed-of-sound (SoS) validation of a ring-array USCT system. The phantoms featured a stable background medium (SoS of 1540 m/s) and embedded cylindrical inclusions of 5 mm and 10 mm diameters with three clinically relevant target SoS values (1475, 1500, and 1510 m/s against a 1540 m/s background). The SoS of all materials was independently characterized by through-transmission measurements, with their SoS confirmed stable by repeated testing over two years. A clinical 2,048-element ring-array USCT system was adopted for data acquisition, and three reconstruction methods (ray-based method, L2-norm full-waveform inversion (L2-FWI), and UNN-FWI) were quantitatively compared. Experimental results demonstrated that UNN-FWI with implicit regularization outperformed conventional methods, exhibiting the lowest area and SoS reconstruction errors for all SoS differences and target sizes. L2-FWI suffered from cycle-skipping artifacts and obvious quantitative underestimation, while ray-based methods showed severe spatial resolution limitations. This work provides a standardized, reusable phantom-based validation framework for USCT SoS imaging. The publicly released datasets further support global algorithm benchmarking, filling the critical gap in USCT quantitative quality assurance and facilitating the clinical translation and standardization of USCT technology.

title: Transthoracic Electromechanical and Mechanical Cardiac Function Imaging in Acute and Chronic Myocardial Infarction Progression.
abstract: Rationale Accurate and precise quantitative functional echocardiographic assessment remains a clinical challenge. Myocardial elastography (ME) and electromechanical wave imaging (EWI) are ultrasound-based elastographic myocardial strain estimation methods that, in tandem, aim to aid in the diagnosis and monitoring of cardiac diseases. Until now, these modalities have been used separately. In this study, we explore their compatibility to localize and detect both the electromechanical and mechanical effects of ischemia. Methods A longitudinal myocardial infarction model was studied in canine subjects (n = 9) for either 4 days (4-d; n = 6) or 5 week (5 wk; n = 3) to investigate the ability of ME and EWI to detect, locate and monitor collateral perfusion recovery from infarction generated via ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD). Canine subjects were imaged with both a 300 frames/s and a 2000 frames/s ultrasound radiofrequency acquisition scheme for ME and EWI, respectively, at baseline, daily (n = 9) for 1 week and on a weekly basis (n = 3) for 4 weeks. Both techniques were performed on the acquired data and then segmented by coronary perfusion region. ME displacements were calculated with 1-D normalized cross-correlation in the axial and lateral directions (4.6 mm window, 80% window overlap, 3× lateral re-correlation), and EWI displacements were calculated with the 1-D normalized cross-correlation (5 mm window, 90% window overlap). Strains were computed using a least-squares estimator, resulting in ME cumulative radial strains and EWI interframe axial strains. The means and standard deviations were calculated by day for each technique and observed for the duration of the study. The differences in the cumulative systolic strain and the systolic activation timings between each treatment day and baseline were calculated between each perfusion segment. Results In the 4-d experiments, the difference between baseline and treatment days was significantly greater in the LAD segment than in the right coronary artery or left circumflex coronary artery (LCX) for both ME (p < 0.005, mixed-effects analysis with Geisser-Greenhouse correction and Tukey's multiple comparisons) and EWI (p < 0.001, mixed-effects analysis with Geisser-Greenhouse correction and Tukey's multiple comparisons). Over the duration of the 4 d study, the LAD showed the most significant electromechanical delay from baseline imaging. The same trend was observed in the 4 wk studies, where the LAD segment showed the most significant difference (ME: -25.8% ± 15.2%; EWI: 58.2 ± 39.5 ms) from baseline for both ME (LCX: -10.0% ± 22.2%, p < 0.01, Kruskal-Wallis test with Dunn's multiple comparisons) and EWI (right coronary artery: 31.4 ± 36.6 ms, p < 0.01, Kruskal-Wallis test with Dunn's multiple comparisons; LCX: 33.6 ± 40.1 ms, p < 0.01, Kruskal-Wallis test with Dunn's multiple comparisons). The LAD segment showed a more significant electromechanical delay between baseline and each treatment day for EWI over the 4 wk studies. This was also observed with an increased EWI systolic activation time delay between baseline and week 4. Conclusions Both ME cumulative radial strain and EWI systolic activation timing showed the ability to monitor myocardial infarction recovery over both an acute (4 d) and a chronic (4 wk) period. ME also showed substantial collateral reperfusion of the canine myocardium in the recovery of radial strain magnitude, while an electromechanical delay remained throughout both phases of the study over the LAD perfusion segment. Taken together, these findings indicate that even after apparent recovery of cumulative radial strain to baseline values, there is a remaining functional deficit in the form of electromechanical activation. EWI showed the ability to complement ME by providing insight into the electromechanical recovery of the myocardium in addition to the radial strain magnitude.

title: Real-Time Prediction of Cardiac Parameters Using Livestream Transthoracic Echocardiography Images: A Feasibility Study.
abstract: The aim of this study is to develop a workflow for acquiring and analyzing livestream echocardiography images from a GE HealthCare Vivid E95 system, a real-time artificial intelligence (AI)-based automatic left ventricle segmentation, and cardiac parameter prediction. The system provides automated echocardiography image analysis independent of electrocardiogram signals. A software pipeline was developed to acquire and analyze livestream echocardiography images from the ultrasound system. A UNet neural network model was trained using publicly available datasets (CAMUS, EchoNet-Dynamic) and an in-house dataset (Physical Activity and Fitness in Childhood Cancer Survivors). AI models were trained using these three datasets and three loss functions, with each model evaluated independently on all three test datasets. The model with the highest Dice score on the test datasets was selected and used to process livestream echocardiography images throughout the entire cardiac cycle. The resulting segmentation masks were used to compute the cardiac parameters. The offline-trained UNet models achieved an average Dice score of 0.9509. The livestream echocardiography image prediction showed average ejection fractions of 48%, 48% and 56%, corresponding to the Simpson's single-plane, area-length and Bullet methods, respectively. In contrast, EchoPAC (the GE HealthCare software tool to compute cardiac parameters) showed an average ejection fraction of 55% in nine volunteers with no known cardiac diseases. This study shows the feasibility of AI-assisted echocardiographic image analysis based on livestream echocardiography. However, the accuracy of the obtained cardiac parameters needs improvement to align with clinical standards.

title: Focused Ultrasound in Parkinson's Disease: From Mechanisms to Precision Therapy.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that markedly impairs motor function and quality of life. As conventional pharmacotherapy and deep brain stimulation are increasingly limited by waning efficacy, treatment-related complications or surgical ineligibility, focused ultrasound (FUS) has emerged as a versatile, non-invasive platform that delivers acoustic energy with high spatiotemporal precision. Prior investigations of FUS for PD have often remained fragmented within two largely disconnected domains: clinical application and laboratory-based mechanistic validation. To bridge the gap between these two disconnected domains, a narrative and translational review was conducted that integrates the latest advances from both fields into a unified framework. A structured literature search of PubMed and Web of Science for articles published between January 2004 and November 2025 was conducted. After applying pre-defined inclusion criteria and exclusion criteria, a total of 114 articles were identified and constitute the evidence base for this review. Reference lists of included articles were manually screened to identify additional relevant publications. Our findings critically benchmark thermal ablation, transcranial ultrasound stimulation and BBB opening against established therapies, while appraising their key technical limitations. Looking forward, this review highlights three engineering trajectories poised to propel the field from empirical trial-and-error toward precision medicine: predictive numerical simulations for individualized treatment planning, standardization of sonication protocols and regulatory frameworks, and the evolution from open-loop to real-time closed-loop intelligent control for personalized adaptive therapy. By integrating mechanistic insights, clinical evidence and emerging technologies, this review provides a comprehensive roadmap for advancing FUS-based precision management of PD.

title: Volumetric Tissue Organization Mapping Using Backscatter Tensor Imaging With a Row Column Addressing Transducer.
abstract: Introduction Alterations in tissue organization are involved in numerous pathologies and may influence disease progression and therapeutic response. Backscatter Tensor Imaging (BTI), an emerging ultrasound (US) technique based on local spatial coherence, can be used to map tissue structure in a whole volume. However, previous volumetric implementations were limited by prolonged acquisition times or required high channel count systems. Row Column Addressing transducers (RCA) achieve volumetric acquisitions with a low channel count, making it potentially compatible with clinical settings, but have never been used for BTI. Here, we aimed to evaluate the feasibility of mapping tissue organization with an RCA probe. Methods This was done using a 6 MHz RCA probe driven by a 256-channel programmable US machine. A rotation motor was used to image the medium at 36 angular positions with respect to a reference position. The local spatial coherence of backscattered signals was calculated at each position, and the coherence values used to determine the medium orientation and fractional anisotropy. This methodology was validated in vitro in a metal needle immersed in water to test for its ability to identify a highly organized medium. We then tested the ability of our method to accurately map complex medium organization in an agar phantom consisting of fishing lines wrapped around a cylindrical structure, and an ex vivo phantom of orthogonally stacked chicken breasts. Results The measured coherence was significantly higher in the organized needle structure than in water (+20.8%, p = 0.0167). In the cylindrical phantom, measured medium orientations at the location of the fishing lines followed the expected circumferential organization, yielding a regression slope of 0.836, a bias of 9.0°, and a regression coefficient R 2 of 0.979. In ex vivo tissue, the measured organization agreed visually with the fiber orientation observed on corresponding tissue sections. Acquisitions required approximately 5 min and covered a cylindrical imaging volume with a radius of 12.8 mm and a depth of 50 mm. Conclusion These results demonstrate the feasibility of volumetric BTI using an RCA transducer for the characterization of medium organization. Future work will focus on eliminating probe rotation to enable more practical clinical implementation.

title: A Dual-configuration Kidney Phantom Platform for Ultrasound-guided Percutaneous Renal Access: Design and Initial Functional Assessment.
abstract: Objective Physical kidney phantoms provide controlled environments for training and technology evaluation in percutaneous renal access (PRA), including image-guided and robot-assisted approaches. This study developed a dual-configuration phantom for ultrasound (US)-guided PRA addressing limitations in geometric representation, collecting-system anatomy, and rib-based access constraints, and performed an initial functional assessment. Methods The kidney model comprises a thin silicone shell, synthetic gel-filled renal compartment, and hollow multicalyceal collecting system. The water-based configuration enabled adjustable kidney positioning and a replaceable puncture membrane, while the gel-based configuration incorporated surrounding material resistance, computed tomography (CT)-derived ribs, and respiratory actuation. Assessment included 2D and 3D US and CT imaging, material sound speed, respiratory motion, combined retrograde and percutaneous instrumentation, qualitative electromagnetic (EM)-US overlay assessment, and experimental use. Results Principal renal and collecting-system interfaces were identifiable in US and CT, while combined retrograde and percutaneous access and EM-US navigation were feasible. Material sound speeds ranged from 1004 to 1490 m/s, and successful collecting-system access was achieved in 94.1% of 188 trials. The water-based configuration supported approximately 120 punctures, with membrane replacement after approximately 40 punctures, while gel-based units were generally replaced after approximately 30. Conclusion The platform supported initial functional feasibility for US-guided PRA, supporting multimodal imaging, combined retrograde and percutaneous workflows, EM-US navigation, respiratory actuation, and repeated experimental use. The two configurations provided complementary levels of adjustability and physical constraint.
